statement: Shortest paths in a graph with negative edge weights can be computed by adding a large enough constant c to every edge weight to make all weights nonnegative, running Dijkstra, and then subtracting c once per edge used along the returned path.
definitions: Directed graph with real edge weights and no negative-weight cycle (so shortest paths are well defined); c is any constant with c >= -(minimum edge weight); the procedure's output is Dijkstra's path in the shifted graph together with its shifted cost minus c times its number of edges; the claim asserts this equals a true shortest path and its cost.
